summary: Port Stanley Breakwater Light, Lake Erie: a concrete tower at the end of the west breakwater, built 1909 to 1910 after an 1881 wooden light; owned by the municipality since 2016.

structures.note: Coast Guard list 10.1 m; Lighthouse Directory 9.5 m (31 ft); the 1910 Department report describes a 27-foot beacon. Built: Lighthouse Friends says completed 1909; the Department's report for the year ended 31 March 1909 shows it under construction.

access.note: Reached only by boat; site and tower closed (Lighthouse Directory). A 2015 news report said the breakwater pier would reopen to walkers that summer; the sources read do not confirm its status after 2015.

facts.agency: Municipality of Central Elgin (owner and site manager); the light is still listed by the Canadian Coast Guard

events.note: Committee of the House of Assembly of Upper Canada recommends funds for lights at Port Stanley, Port Burwell and the Cut at Long Point (Lighthouse Friends).
First lighthouse built on the harbour pier (Register). Earlier light, not the present tower.
A vessel entering the harbour in a gale struck and destroyed the light (Lighthouse Friends; no second source read).
Lantern with four lamps and fourteen-inch reflectors hoisted onto a frame by Keeper Charles Ead, probably in 1876 (Lighthouse Friends).

Wooden square tower on the outer end of the west breakwater, fixed white catoptric light, built by John Ellison under a $1,250 contract (contract 1881; Lighthouse Friends quotes the Department's description).
Reinforced concrete tower on the government breakwater, built by contract by F. R. Miller of Port Stanley for $3,850 (Lighthouse Friends: completed 1909).
Acetylene gas beacon on the breakwater, showing a fixed red light (year ended 31 March 1910).
Light changed from a fixed red to a white light, occulted at short intervals (year ended 31 March 1911).
One-inch diaphone fog signal installed (Lighthouse Friends). Not confirmed in the Department reports read.
Shore light established to form a range with the breakwater light; the west pier mast light changed from white to green (Lighthouse Friends).

Port Stanley life-boat crew, coxswain J. R. Moore, with the tug Gordon Brown, rescued five men from the schooner Mineral State (wrecked in a gale south of the harbour). The entry gives no date; it is in the report for the year ended 30 June 1902.

December 1909 (the year ended 31 March 1910 life-saving report): the Port Stanley lifeboat went to assist the Astahula, which had gone ashore at Port Burwell, a different harbour; her crew refused to leave, and she was got off, with compensation from the company.
Pier closed to pedestrians after three young men died at the site in June 1998 (news report, 2015).
Transport Canada transferred ownership of the pier and harbour to the municipality, with a one-time payout of $13.6 million (September 2010).
Breakwater rehabilitation under way, with barriers and handrails, and a planned reopening to walkers later that summer (news report).
Lighthouse deed received by the Municipality of Central Elgin, with a one-time $65,000 grant for restoration and upkeep.
Designated a heritage lighthouse under the Heritage Lighthouse Protection Act.

wrecks.outcome: Wrecked in a gale and heavy sea a short way south of the Port Stanley harbour; the coxswain J. R. Moore and a volunteer life-boat crew, with the tug Gordon Brown, rescued five men exposed for five hours. Entry gives no date (year ended 30 June 1902).
Struck and destroyed the harbour light while entering in a gale. Lighthouse Friends only; no other source read confirms it.

corrections.why: The record's light values are those of the Port Stanley East Breakwater light (entry 587: Fl R 4s, 9.1 m). The breakwater light this record describes is entry 588: Fl G 5s, with 11.5 m focal height and a 5 nautical mile range.
Entry 588 (Port Stanley Breakwater) gives 11.5 m; 9.1 m is the East Breakwater light's focal height (entry 587).

Entry 588 is at 42 39 18.6 N, 081 12 48.3 W. The record's current position is within about 3 m of entry 587 (East Breakwater, 42 39 21.1 N, 081 12 43.4 W). The record's own tower location (42.655165, -81.213387) matches entry 588.

notes_for_editor: Build date: the record gives 1911 (from the Parks Canada data) and the Directory gives 1908; Lighthouse Friends says completed 1909; the Department's report for the year ended 31 March 1909 shows the tower under construction and the year ended 31 March 1910 lists the acetylene beacon. A search excerpt of the Register page gives 'Built in 1911' and '10 metres (33 feet)', but the Register text the tool could read contains neither, so the story gives no Register date. Please check the Register's description section. Height: 27 feet (Department 1910), 9.5 m (31 ft, Directory), 10.1 m (Coast Guard), 10.0 m (record). The record has two structure entries for the same tower (the 10.0 m Parks Canada tower and the 10.1 m Coast Guard entry 'Port Stanley Breakwater', located on a separate OSM node); consider merging. Corrections: the record's characteristic, focal height and location are the East Breakwater light's values (entry 587), see corrections. Keepers: the Lighthouse Friends head-keeper list covers the Port Stanley light from before the 1909 tower; whether the breakwater tower was staffed separately is not established. Mrs. Charles Ead's first name is not in the sources read. Lighthouse Friends' 1876 sentence on Charles Ead's salary ('raised to $275 from $300') reads as a decrease and is not used. The 1861 loss rests on Lighthouse Friends alone; a Chronicling America search for 1861 to 1862 found no report of it. The 1913 diaphone is Lighthouse Friends only (no Department report read mentions it). Breakwater access: the 2015 news report said the pier would reopen to walkers; the Directory (undated) says the site is reachable only by boat. The status after 2015 is not confirmed; a 2026 municipal tender for breakwater work turned up in search but was not read. The 1998 deaths are given as the news report gives them (three young men, June 1998; no names, no cause). The Mineral State entry gives no date; the 1902 report year is used. The Coast Guard list gives the East Breakwater light a red flash (Fl R 4s) and the breakwater light a green flash (Fl G 5s). No photos were checked. Fact-check 2026-10-27: the 1910 life-saving report (year 1909-10) records a second Port Stanley lifeboat service, the Astahula, ashore at Port Burwell in December 1909; it is now in the story and as an event (source 13, scan 206, printed 204). The 1907 keeper statement was checked on the page image: 'Ead, Mrs. C. / Port Stanley / May 15, 1890' on printed page 164 (scan 174 in the PDF; the archive's page/n173 viewer index). The Oliver row (1912 volume) is a single OCR line (station, name, date), not matched by column. A 1911 life-saving inspection note on the Port Stanley station (no rescue) is not used.
